cards.text: Friend, buckle up, because Judah is about to go through kings faster than I go through chocolate chips. King Josiah is dead. The people of the land take one of his sons and make him king in Jerusalem in his father's place.

cards.question: Which of Josiah's sons do the people of the land make king in Jerusalem?
Jehoahaz is twenty-three years old when he becomes king. He reigns in Jerusalem for three ___.

cards.text: Three MONTHS. Friend, that's not a reign, that's a FREE TRIAL! And the trial ends when the king of Egypt dethrones him right there in Jerusalem.

cards.question: After dethroning Jehoahaz, the king of Egypt makes Judah pay a levy of a hundred talents of gold.

cards.text: Now Neco, king of Egypt, makes Eliakim, the brother of Jehoahaz, king over Judah and Jerusalem. And Neco doesn't just hand him a crown, he hands him a whole new name.

cards.question: What new name does Neco give Eliakim when he makes him king over Judah?

cards.text: Meanwhile, Jehoahaz is off the throne. And Neco isn't leaving him in Jerusalem.

cards.question: Neco, king of Egypt, takes Jehoahaz and carries him off to Babylon.

cards.text: Jehoiakim is twenty-five when he becomes king, and he reigns in Jerusalem eleven years. After his brother's three months, ELEVEN YEARS is a lifetime achievement award!

cards.question: King Jehoiakim does what is right in the sight of the LORD his God.

cards.text: Then Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, comes up against Jehoiakim and binds him with bronze shackles to take him to Babylon. He also takes some of the articles from the house of the LORD.

cards.question: Nebuchadnezzar takes articles from the house of the LORD to Babylon and puts them in his ___.

cards.text: The rest of Jehoiakim's story, abominations and all, is written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah. Then his son takes the throne.

cards.question: Jehoiakim's son ___ reigns in his place.

cards.text: Jehoiachin is eighteen when he becomes king, and just like his father, he does evil in the sight of the LORD. Now watch how long he lasts.

cards.question: How long does Jehoiachin reign in Jerusalem?

cards.text: Three months and ten days, friend, and that's ten whole days longer than his uncle got! In the spring, Nebuchadnezzar summons Jehoiachin and brings him to Babylon, along with the articles of value from the house of the LORD.

cards.question: Who does Nebuchadnezzar make king over Judah and Jerusalem after Jehoiachin?

cards.text: Zedekiah is twenty-one when he becomes king, and he reigns in Jerusalem eleven years. He does evil in the sight of the LORD his God, and there's a prophet speaking for the LORD right there: Jeremiah.

cards.question: King Zedekiah humbles himself before Jeremiah the prophet.

cards.text: Here's the thing. King Nebuchadnezzar had made Zedekiah swear by God.

cards.question: Zedekiah swore by God to King Nebuchadnezzar. So what does Zedekiah do?

answers.text: He keeps his oath to him
He asks him for an army

cards.text: Zedekiah stiffens his neck and hardens his heart against turning to the LORD. Friend, that is NOT a posture problem.

The leaders of the priests and the people multiply their unfaithful deeds and defile the house of the LORD. And still, again and again, the LORD, the God of their fathers, sends word to His people through His messengers.

cards.question: Why does the LORD keep sending messengers to His people again and again?

answers.text: They asked Him for a sign

cards.question: The LORD keeps sending messengers because He has compassion on His people. How do the people treat those messengers?

answers.text: They mock and scoff at them

cards.text: They keep despising His words until the wrath of the LORD against His people is stirred up beyond remedy. So He brings up the king of the Chaldeans against them.

cards.question: God gives His people all into the hand of the king of the Chaldeans, ___.

cards.text: Young men are put to the sword in the sanctuary, sparing neither young nor old. Nebuchadnezzar carries off everything to Babylon, from the articles of the house of God to the treasures of the king and his officials.

cards.question: The Chaldeans set fire to the house of God.

cards.text: They break down the wall of Jerusalem and burn down all the palaces. Those who escaped the sword are carried off to Babylon to serve Nebuchadnezzar and his sons.

cards.question: The exiles stay servants to Nebuchadnezzar and his sons until the kingdom of ___ comes to power.
Back home, the land enjoys its Sabbath rest all the days of the desolation, until ___ years are completed, fulfilling the word of the LORD spoken through Jeremiah.

cards.text: Now it's the first year of Cyrus, king of Persia. And the word of the LORD spoken through Jeremiah is about to be fulfilled.

cards.question: Cyrus, king of Persia, sends a proclamation throughout his kingdom and puts it in writing. Who stirred his spirit to do it?
In his proclamation, Cyrus says the LORD, the God of heaven, has given him all the kingdoms of the earth. What does Cyrus say the LORD appointed him to do?

answers.text: Build Him a house at Jerusalem

cards.question: Cyrus tells anyone who belongs to the LORD's people that they may go up.

cards.text: Seventy years of desolation, and I thought MY stretch in the junk drawer was long! Now the LORD stirs a king of Persia to open the door, and His people can go up to Jerusalem to build His house.

findings.problem: Most of Stop 1's choice cards are discovery questions that can only be answered by luck. These include which son is made king (card 2), months vs. years vs. weeks (card 3), silver vs. gold in the levy (card 5), Eliakim's new name (card 7), Egypt vs. Babylon for Jehoahaz (card 9), temple vs. palace vs. treasury (card 13), the name of Jehoiakim's son (card 15) and the name Nebuchadnezzar gives the next king (card 19). Very few cards in the stop are informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: 'King Josiah is dead' is a fact from outside the passage (2 Chronicles 35:24). 36:1 only says Jehoahaz was made king in place of his father. The card cites only 2 Chronicles 36:1, so the outside fact has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card asks about the exact makeup of Egypt's levy (talents of silver vs. gold). That detail doesn't move the passage forward and isn't needed to understand it.

rule.text: Ask about the moments that move the passage forward and the details the baker needs to understand it.

findings.problem: 'Now watch how long he lasts' signals a surprisingly short reign. Card 17 has only one short answer ('Three months and ten days'), so the setup rules out the two long wrong answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This last story card recaps 36:21-23, which cards 15 through 19 have already covered (the seventy years, the LORD stirring Cyrus, going up to Jerusalem). It doesn't move the passage forward.

'His people can go up to Jerusalem to build His house' connects the people's going up with the building. 36:23 says the LORD appointed Cyrus to build the house, and separately says His people may go up. The passage never says the people go up to build.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
